knownReferenceChecks.opcodeAdjacentClassification: Bounded heuristic only. These are opcode-adjacent byte patterns whose apparent 16-bit operands fall inside the range; they are not decoded native or VM references and are not proof of execution or use.

opcodeAdjacentMethod.description: Scans bank-0 offsets 1000-FFFD for the listed opcode bytes and treats the following big-endian 16-bit value as an apparent absolute operand; records matches whose value lies in 1010-13EF.
limitations: No instruction-length decoding; an opcode byte may be an immediate, data or operand byte, as in LDX #$03FE.
Does not distinguish loads from stores, direct/indexed modes, branch targets, threaded-VM tokens or reachability.
Writes to ROM addresses do not read candidate bytes and are not references.
Matches are unresolved heuristics, not decoded references.

referenceInventoryMethod.native: Regex scan for four-hex-digit tokens in curated evidence/mpu4/native/*.json assembly text.
referenceInventoryMethod.vm: Regex scan for four-hex-digit tokens in curated evidence/mpu4/VM-SCRIPTS/*.txt lines no longer than 400 characters.
limitations: Textual token scans are not a complete disassembler or a decoded reference graph.
The curated listings are incomplete and may contain non-address four-hex-digit values.
Zero decoded matches is not a complete no-use proof.
